sections.h2: Who bills property tax in White Plains
sections.html:
The City of White Plains Finance Department bills and collects at City Hall, 255 Main Street, Room 102. The City Assessor sets the values the bill is based on. White Plains is the seat of Westchester County, and one household can receive a city and school bill in July and January, and a county bill in April.

Bills are made out to the owner of record. Under RPTL 922, a bill that never reaches the owner does not cancel the tax or stop penalties and interest from running. If one fails to arrive, call 914-422-1248 so the address can be verified and a duplicate mailed.

  • Finance Department: payments, bill copies, address changes and payoff figures. The city lists 914-422-1235 for tax office questions.
  • Assessor, 255 Main Street, phone 914-422-1223: assessed value, exemptions, parcel information and complaint forms.
  • Board of Assessment Review: hears complaints that an assessment is unequal, excessive or misclassified.

Taxes come due three times a year: July 1 and January 1 for city and school tax, and April 1 for county tax. The city allows payment through the last day of each month without interest, so the practical deadlines are July 31, January 31 and April 30.

Bills are mailed in mid-December, late March and June. Payments must be postmarked or hand-delivered by the due date, or they carry interest. Overdue tax and water charges accrue interest at 1 percent a month, and state law gives the city no power to waive that interest for any reason.

sections.h2: Ways to pay a White Plains bill
sections.html:
You can pay in person, online, by mail or by automatic debit. City Hall accepts payments from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on days other than holidays, at the Finance Department window in Room 102.

  • Mail with the stub: make the check out to the Commissioner of Finance and send it to P.O. Box 5086, White Plains, NY 10602-5086.
  • Mail without the stub: send the check to the Finance Department at 255 Main Street, Room 102, and write your section, block and lot number on it.
  • Online: the city runs a portal for tax and water payments by credit card.
  • Direct payment: sign an authorization agreement and the city debits a checking or savings account when each installment is due.

Ownership changes are recorded by the Assessor, who needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address for billing goes in on the Tax Account Change Form. Owners can also name a consenting third party to receive copies of bills, using the Third Party Notification Form.

sections.h2: How to challenge a White Plains assessment
sections.html:
File a complaint on form RP-524 between January 1 and January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review. The Board meets on January 21 under the City Charter. On Thursday, January 21, 2027 it sits by appointment from 3 to 5 p.m. and 7 to 9 p.m. in the Common Council Chambers, Room 203, at City Hall. Call 914-422-1223 to book a time.

White Plains runs on a different calendar from towns that hold a May grievance day. The taxable status date is December 1, the tentative roll is January 1, the final roll is March 1, and exemptions are processed from April 1 through December 1. A late complaint loses the right to review, so mark January on the calendar before you list.

Bring evidence of market value, such as recent sales of comparable homes nearby or an appraisal. The Board decides whether an assessment is unequal, excessive or in the wrong class.

sections.h2: How a White Plains tax bill is figured
sections.html:
Two things set it: the property's taxable assessment and the levies of the jurisdictions that tax it. The tax rate is the levy divided by the total taxable assessed value, and the assessment reflects the property's value less any exemptions the owner qualifies for.

That is why an exemption can change a bill without touching the city's budget. The Assessor processes exemption applications from April 1 through December 1 each year. Ask the Assessor which exemptions are on your parcel before you give a buyer a bill to rely on.

Unpaid water charges do not disappear. They are relevied against the property as a tax lien on the following July 1. A seller with an old water balance can therefore find it folded into the next tax bill and into the payoff.

Residential water in the city is divided into six districts, each billed twice a year, and a final water reading costs $75 when requested by calling 914-422-1211. Schedule the reading with the closing so the water account closes cleanly and the buyer starts with a clear record. If the property has water service, an available-on-demand charge based on meter size is billed even when no water is used.

The city had 62,871 residents in July 2025. Owners hold 51.0 percent of homes, so renters are nearly half of households, and the 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $620,800. Median monthly owner costs run $3,525 with a mortgage and $1,494 without one, and median gross rent is $2,269.

The city covers only 9.74 square miles of land, so a sale price on the next street over is often a better guide than any citywide median.

sections.h2: Selling a White Plains house with tax due
sections.html:
Ask the Finance Department for a payoff that includes city, school, county and any water relevy, and confirm the date to which interest is calculated. A few steps keep the sale clean.

  • Check which of the July, January and April installments are paid.
  • Ask whether any water charges were relevied on a July 1 bill.
  • Make sure the Assessor has the current deed and owner name on file.
  • If you plan to contest the value, file by January 21, since a late complaint loses the right to review.

A cash buyer can close with open tax, and the title company pays the balance from the proceeds. Since interest is 1 percent each month, a closing date that slips past month end changes the number.

faqs.q: When are White Plains property taxes due?
faqs.a: City and school tax is due July 1 and January 1, and county tax is due April 1. The city accepts payment through the last day of each of those months, and interest applies after that.

faqs.q: What is the White Plains late interest rate?
faqs.a: It is 1 percent a month on overdue taxes and water charges. State law prevents the Finance Department from waiving interest or penalties on a late payment.

faqs.q: When is White Plains grievance day?
faqs.a: There is no May grievance day. Complaints are filed January 1 through January 21 with the Assessor or the Board of Assessment Review, which meets on January 21 by appointment. Call 914-422-1223.

faqs.q: Can I set up automatic payments for White Plains taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Sign and return the city's authorization agreement to the Finance Department at 255 Main Street, Room 102. The city then debits your checking or savings account on each due date.

faqs.q: How do I change the owner name on a White Plains tax bill?
faqs.a: Only the Assessor's Office can record a change of ownership, and it needs a certified copy of the recorded deed. A change of mailing address goes through the Tax Account Change Form.
